text: Laughed so hard at dinner with Ines and Tomás that the waiter came over to check on us.
Nothing special happened, honestly. I just felt light all day, like someone opened a window in my chest.
Not a huge feeling, just pleasant. Coffee was good, inbox was quiet, I left on time.
Wedding rehearsal for Priya and Sean. Everything went wrong in the funniest ways and nobody cared. I love these people.
Yesterday I was a mess about the presentation. Today it went great and three people asked for my slides. What a difference a day makes.
We finally painted the bedroom. Sage green. It feels like a new home.
Kids' drawing on the fridge says 'best mum in the univers'. Leaving the spelling exactly as it is forever.
Office birthday cake for me, organised by Gemma. I didn't think anyone knew. Felt really seen.
Dad finally tried the curry I've been perfecting and asked for seconds. He never asks for seconds.
New glasses. I can see individual leaves on the trees again. I didn't know how blurry everything had become.
Book club picked my suggestion and everyone loved it, even Harold who hates everything.
Our little choir sang at the care home. One woman sang along to every word with her eyes closed.
Watched Ben's train pull out. Six months until I see him again. Walked home the long way so I wouldn't have to be in the flat yet.
Clearing out the nursery we never used. Folded every tiny onesie and put them in a box for the charity shop.
Rainy Sunday. Listened to the album Callum and I used to play on road trips. Should not have done that.
My manuscript came back with a form rejection. Forty-one now. Some days I can laugh about it. Not today.
Kenji's leaving the team. Best boss I've had. Smiled through his speech and then sat in the stairwell for a bit.
Saw a dad and his little girl feeding ducks and had to look away. Some days the wanting is a lot.
The old dog next door, the one who always barked hello, wasn't at the gate today. Mrs. Bello told me he died on Friday.
Mateus forgot my birthday. Small thing. Didn't feel small.
I read the old diary from when I was 14 and just felt so sorry for her. She had no idea how hard things were going to get.
Put the 'For Sale' sign on the boat Pop and I restored together. Couldn't stand next to it while the buyers looked.
The adoption fell through at the last minute. The birth mother changed her mind. I understand. I'm devastated.
Biopsy results come back Thursday. I've checked the portal eleven times today even though I know they won't be there yet.
The lump is probably nothing, the GP said, but she wants a scan to be sure. 'To be sure' is doing a lot of work in that sentence.
Our daughter came home from her party an hour late and wouldn't say where she'd been. I'm trying not to imagine things.
Started the new meds today. Doctor said the first week can be rough. Every little twinge I'm wondering if it's a side effect.
Court date for the custody hearing is next month. I'm trying to keep things normal for the kids but I'm shaking inside.
Slight dread about the family dinner. Uncle Viktor will bring up politics. He always does.
Driving on the motorway for the first time since the accident. Made it. Hands were slippery on the wheel the whole way.
Third night in a row of nightmares about missing a train. Waking with my heart going like a drum.
I froze in the meeting when Carla asked me a direct question. Now replaying it on loop and imagining what everyone thinks.
Pregnancy test in the bathroom. Two minutes. Longest two minutes of my life. Not sure which answer I'm hoping for.
Restless and worried all day about the money, the job, my knee, everything at once and nothing in particular.
Sat in the car outside the house for five minutes before going in. Not avoiding anything, just enjoying the quiet.
Steady day. Did my work, ate well, went to bed early. Nothing to report and that's a nice feeling.
Was expecting to be nervous before the operation but I felt surprisingly calm. The nurse, Bridget, held my hand and talked about her garden.
Not stressed for once. Work's under control, flat's tidy, nothing urgent.
The kids are asleep, the dishes are done, the house is warm. I'm just sitting here listening to the fridge hum.
The train was delayed and instead of getting cross I just read my book. Growth?
I let the phone ring out and finished my tea. It can wait. Everything can wait for ten minutes.
Sat on the hill behind the house and watched the sheep for half an hour. Mind as empty as the sky.
Gentle day. Baked bread, called Auntie Grace, folded laundry in the sun.
Slow coffee with Martina on her stoop, watching the street wake up.
Cleared my inbox to zero, then shut the laptop and sat in the garden. Mind tidy as the inbox.
Rereading the messages everyone sent after the surgery. I didn't realise how many people care.
My therapist, Dana, said 'you did the hard thing'. I'm so thankful I found her.
Thank you, coffee. Thank you, quiet Saturday. Thank you, whoever invented the electric blanket.
Gran left me her sewing machine. Every time I use it I feel her hands on mine.
Got through the interview because Leon spent all weekend doing mock questions with me.
Tamsin and Freddie looked after the dog for two weeks and sent daily photos. He's clearly been spoiled.
The surgeon, Mr. Adebayo, explained everything slowly and drew me a diagram. I felt like a person not a case number.
So thankful for Wi-Fi calls. Saw my niece take her first steps from 4,000 miles away.
Sundar spotted the mistake in my report before it went to the client. Saved my skin.
Grateful that the fever broke overnight. She's watching cartoons and asking for toast.
I'm stuck. Six months at this job and I'm doing exactly what I did on day one. No growth, no plan, no feedback.
Ugh. Planned a whole day of writing and got nothing done except reorganising my bookshelf.
Lost again at chess to Ivan. Same opening trap. Every. Single. Time.
The groceries were delivered to the wrong flat and now I'm making dinner out of crackers and hope.
Lovely, the car failed its MOT. On my birthday. Perfect timing as always.
The software update moved every button I use. Spent half the morning hunting for 'export'.
Spent my day off fixing someone else's mistake. Again.
I tried to talk to Pilar about how I've been feeling and she turned it into a story about herself.
Every form wants a utility bill and I don't have one in my name because I just moved. Catch-22.
I want to move forward and every door I push on is locked. That's this whole month.
Can't sleep, too buzzed about the hackathon. We have the idea. We have the team. Let's go.
Wedding in three weeks. Dress fitting today. Seeing it all come together gave me chills.
Gig at the pub on Friday. Our first ever with people who aren't related to us.
Yesterday felt flat but today I've got that fizzy feeling about the trip again.
Orientation week! So many clubs. Signed up for climbing, debate and something called 'competitive cheese tasting'.
Countdown to the eclipse: four days. We're driving to the path of totality and I have the special glasses.
Applying for the master's programme and actually excited for the first time in ages about what's next.
Little thrill reading the itinerary for the work trip. Lisbon for three days. I haven't travelled in years.
Our first holiday as a family of four. Suitcases on the bed. Kids already wearing swimsuits indoors.
New season of our show drops at midnight. Kemal and I have strict rules: no spoilers, no phones.
Started learning Spanish with an app and I want to practise all the time. Ordering coffee in Spanish next month in Seville!
I'm starting to see that the version of success I chased in my twenties was mostly someone else's.
I'm the same age Dad was when I was born. Strange to think of him at 34, as unsure as me.
Talking with Bilal about faith made me realise mine changed shape rather than disappeared.
Wondering what home means now. The house where I grew up is sold. My flat feels temporary. Maybe it's people, not places.
A year since the diagnosis. I measure time differently now. Before and after.
Watched the documentary about my hometown and saw it through outsiders' eyes. It's smaller and kinder than I remember.
I notice I describe my week by what I achieved and never by how I felt. Trying to change the question.
Hard to know if I'm growing apart from the old crowd or growing into myself. Same thing maybe.
First anniversary of moving in with Nico. Learned a lot about compromise. And towels. So many opinions about towels.
Thinking about Ayodele's advice: 'decide who you are, then the decisions get easier'.
Lunch with Mrs. Oduya, my first boss, retired now. She remembered things about my early career I'd forgotten. Made me see how far I've come.
Things are still hard but I can see a way through now. That's new.
New year, clean notebook. I have a feeling this one will be kinder.
The council finally agreed to look at the crossing outside the school. Maybe the petition worked.
Pavel wrote back. Short message, but friendly. Maybe the friendship isn't over after all.
The new teacher, Mr. Okonkwo, seems to really get my daughter. Fingers crossed this year is easier for her.
I had a real laugh today for the first time since Maya passed. It felt like a sign that life goes on.
The company is restructuring but my manager says my role looks safe. Trying to trust that.
Every small step counts, Ingrid keeps telling me. Today I believed her.
Grief is still here but it's softer this month. I can see a future with joy in it.
Moved the last box into the new place. It's empty and echoing and full of possibility.
Interview went well. Panel smiled a lot. Trying not to read into it. Reading into it.
Covering for two people at work this week. Getting home at nine. Barely talking to Sami.
Chemo week. Body heavy. Sleeping on the sofa most of the day. Lily brought me broth.
Social battery completely drained after the conference. Three days of small talk. Need a quiet weekend.
Too tired to write much. Good day though.
Exhausted from holding it together for everyone at the funeral. Now that they've gone I can barely stand.
Woke up tired, stayed tired, going to bed tired.
The festival was amazing and I am now seventy years old.
Late flight, delayed baggage, taxi queue. Got home at 3am and slept in my clothes.
Exhausted from the long-distance call schedule. Talking to Adaeze at midnight, working at eight.
Long, heavy week. I'm going to sit in the bath until I turn into a prune.
Duncan called me 'sweetheart' in front of the client and then talked over me for the rest of the meeting. I am livid.
Furious at the landlord. He let himself into the flat without notice. Again.
The doctor dismissed my pain AGAIN. 'Probably stress.' I've had this for a year.
Someone stole the bike from right outside the station. Cut the lock. In daylight.
Saw a man kick his dog in the park. Shouted at him. Hands still trembling.
Got overcharged by the mechanic, then he refused to show me the old part. I'm reporting him.
The school cancelled the trip because two parents complained. Thirty kids devastated. I'm so angry for them.
Livid that Marco cancelled my shift without asking and gave it to his friend.
Someone left their dog in a hot car outside the shops. Called the police. Waited with the dog. Seething.
I'm angry, and I'm allowed to be angry. They broke the promise they made to the kids.
After everything I did for Yasmin, she didn't even invite me to the wedding.
Life is pretty good right now. Not exciting. Just good.
Finished the book I've been savouring all month. Satisfying ending. Made tea and just sat with it.
Retirement is suiting me. Garden, crosswords, lunch with Sheila on Wednesdays.
Cosy evening. Soup, socks, the cat purring. I have everything I need.
Our little bookshop had a steady day. Regulars came in, Mr. Fischer bought his usual detective novel.
Ate the first tomato from the garden standing in the sun. Salt in my pocket. Life is good.
I think I've finally found my people. Book club, the Thursday runners, Lin and Jae next door.
Good meal, good friend, good chat. Mehmet always makes me feel at home.
The new job is fine. Nice people, fair pay, home by six. I'm content with fine.
Watching the cricket with Dad, half asleep, the radio on low. Life doesn't get much better.
I've made peace with the ordinary. Turns out I quite like it.
Christmas alone this year. Told everyone I'm fine. Watching carols on the TV with a microwave meal.
Feeling invisible. Nobody noticed I'd been away for a week.
Messaged four friends to see if anyone wanted to get dinner. Two read it. None replied.
Ten days in hospital and the only visitor was the chaplain. Kind man. Still.
First night in the empty house after Esi moved out. Even the fridge sounds loud.
I don't fit in here. Not with the parents at the school gate, not at work, not anywhere really.
Night shift on the ward, the patients asleep, the corridors humming. Very alone tonight.
Lonely in a crowded house. Five of us and nobody talks.
Missing connection. Real connection, not likes.
I miss Callie. Not the relationship, just her. Her company.
Missing my brother tonight. He used to live round the corner. Now he's an ocean away.
Finished my first marathon. 4:41. Cried at the finish line. I did that.
The app I built is live. 300 users in the first day. Strangers using a thing I made!
Finally said no to an extra project. Nobody died. Growth.
Passed the citizenship test. Studied for months in my second language.
I called the doctor about the thing I've been avoiding for months. Appointment booked. Adulting.
First painting sold at the market. To a stranger! For real money!
The patient I've been working with for months walked out of rehab on his own today. I helped make that happen.
My little brother got his first job and called me before anyone else. I helped him write his CV.
Organised the whole conference. 400 people. No disasters. Everyone thanked me.
The student who said she hated reading asked me for book recommendations. Teaching win.
Proud of Lucia for leaving that job. It took real courage.
Thesis due in a month, data analysis not done, supervisor on leave. Spiralling.
Flooded basement, insurance calls, neighbours asking for help with theirs. Haven't slept.
The doctor gave me so much information about the diagnosis I couldn't take any of it in.
Can't think straight. Too many tabs open in my brain.
Packing up the house to sell. Thirty years of stuff. Every drawer is a memory and a decision.
Group project, solo project, part-time job, Mira's birthday. I keep writing lists and losing them.
Everything feels like too much lately. Even small things like replying to messages.
Volunteering, coaching, the PTA, work. I'm the person who can't say no and it's catching up with me.
The festival was amazing but so loud and crowded. I needed to leave halfway.
Election, war, climate. My feed is too much. Deleted the app for a week.
Big family gathering, everyone talking at once, kids running everywhere. Loved it, needed a lie-down after.
Had lunch with Moritz. He's switching teams in June. We talked about the new office layout.
Not much to say today. Fine, I suppose.
Met with Ms. Varga for the parent-teacher conference. Grades are steady. Need to practise spelling.
Today I mostly sat at my desk and worked through tickets. Closed nine.
Assembled the new chair. Took forty minutes.
Jogged around the park. 5k in 31 minutes. Same route as usual.
Sorted out the bookshelf by colour. Took about an hour.
Mum phoned. Talked about the weather and her neighbour's new fence.
Had a check-in with Jordan. Updated the project timeline. Deadline moved to the 20th.
Walked the dog twice, cooked rice and beans, read before bed.
Took inventory of the pantry. Need flour, oil and tinned tomatoes.
Oh brilliant, the flight's delayed four hours. Love airports. Love this plastic chair. Love the eleven-euro sandwich.
Next Friday I'll know about the job. Until then, normal life, apparently.

I'm trying to work out why I feel so flat when on paper the week went well. I finished the project. The client was pleased. Hamid and I had a nice dinner on Thursday. My mum's test results were normal. And still, all week, I've had this grey feeling sitting on my chest, like I'm watching my own life through a window. I don't think it's sadness exactly, more like nothing reaches me. I slept badly most nights. I didn't go to the gym. I've cancelled plans with friends twice. I noticed today that I haven't listened to music in weeks, and music is usually the first thing I reach for. Writing it down makes it look more serious than it felt. Maybe I should mention it to someone.
Grandma taught me her bread recipe today. My hands, her hands, the same dough.
Baked bread with Grandma. She showed me how she kneads it. Felt like being handed something precious.
Tried the new place, Mama Rosa's. Pizza was average. Service was slow. Won't go back.
Absolutely thrilled to be spending my birthday at the tax office. Truly.
Never been less excited about a holiday. Need it, don't want it.
Spent the afternoon at the cemetery tidying Mum's grave. Planted primroses. Talked to her for a while about the kids. It was peaceful, not sad.
